201	crosses and such; slowly, slowly, until in the end they convert them to Christianity.
202	There are videos of the missionaries baptizing people in Tiberias, in the Kinneret, stories, Shema
203	Yisrael.
204	Like the Crusades — there were eight or nine Crusades. In Judaism there is nothing like that. What were the
205	Crusades?
206	The desire to convert the whole world to Christianity — that was the Crusades until now.
207	In Islam there is jihad, to turn everyone into Muslims; in Christianity
208	there is mission, to turn everyone Christian; in Judaism there is no parallel. There is no
209	parallel to this phenomenon in Judaism. Why?
210	On the contrary.
211	The Gemara in Yevamot 47a says: a convert who comes to convert, we tell him, "No need, why are you coming?"
212	Do you know that it is called Sinai because hatred came down to the world?
213	We are persecuted, they hate us, they kill us, they destroy us, we are at the
214	bottom, we have no support anywhere in the world, we only flatter the whole world
215	and take beatings from every direction, whether diplomatically or in practice.
216	So why would you need to... we push the convert away, we don't want him at all. We learned this from Naomi, who said
217	to Ruth, "Go, return, each woman to her mother's house; may HaShem deal kindly with you, as you have dealt with the dead and with me." Afterwards she says to them
218	again, "Go, return, my daughters." Three times in Megillat Ruth, chapter 1, she pushes them away. We don't want
219	converts. On the contrary, Chazal say in Tractate Kiddushin 70b: "Converts are as hard
220	for Israel as a scab."
221	We need righteous converts.
222	If one comes, we accept him.
223	We pray for him.
224	"Upon the righteous, upon the pious, upon the remnant of Your people Israel, and upon the righteous converts."
225	Those are the ones who converted for the sake of Heaven.
226	He has the further merit of having entered the people of Israel.
227	Don't bother telling me we don't accept converts.
228	Nothing of the sort.
229	In the future to come, converts are not accepted in the days of Mashiach.
230	Whoever merited it entered the people of Israel.
231	Now whoever did not merit it is out of luck.
232	In the days of Mashiach, when we have the upper hand, it's clear they will want to convert.
233	As happened on Purim: "Many of the peoples of the land became Jews, for
234	the fear of the Jews fell upon them."
235	The verse gives the reason why they converted, why they became Jews:
236	"For the fear of the Jews fell upon them."
237	Not because they had a deep understanding that HaShem is God, but because
238	the fear of the Jews fell upon them. In the future to come, when we have the upper hand, HaShem will send us the unconventional
239	weapon called our righteous Mashiach, who "with the breath of his lips will slay the wicked."
